title: Surjective zeroth cohomology reduction from first residue vanishing
statement: Let R be a commutative local ring with residue field k. Let C be a cochain complex of R-modules [def-pc-derived-category], supported between integers a and b, with finite free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define the residue complex by extension of scalars to k followed by restriction to R; define the reduction map on cohomology using the extension-restriction adjunction unit. If the first cohomology of the residue complex is zero, this canonical reduction map is surjective in degree zero. No reducedness or other cohomology vanishing is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07VK, residue-vector lifting using the minimal local complex of algebra.tex Tag 00MT

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-finite-free-minimal-model] to replace C by a bounded finite free minimal complex D. Extension and restriction of scalars preserve homotopies, so they preserve this homotopy equivalence and its cohomology isomorphisms.

All residue differentials of D vanish: each image lies in the maximal ideal times the target, and these scalars act by zero in k. Exactness of the residue complex in degree one therefore makes its degree-one term zero. Nakayama (Mathlib IsLocalRing.subsingleton_tensorProduct) makes D^1 zero.

Every vector of D^0 is a cycle. The map D^0 to its residue term is surjective: for a pure tensor r tensor x, lift r through R to k and move it to the x factor; use tensor induction for sums. Hence the induced map of cycles and the induced map of cohomology are surjective. Naturality of the extension-restriction unit transports surjectivity through the two homotopy-equivalence cohomology isomorphisms back to C.

theorem surjective_residueCohomologyMap_zero {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    [C.IsStrictlyGE a] [C.IsStrictlyLE b]
    [∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (C.X i)] [∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R (C.X i)]
    (hH : Subsingleton (C.residueComplex.homology 1)) :
    Function.Surjective (C.residueCohomologyMap 0)
